requirement: Commands, help, version, and invalid option combinations are deterministic
Exit codes distinguish convergence, required action, and operational failure
Strict YAML, discovery boundary, and config-relative paths
CLI precedence, locator inference, and command-specific target requirements
Credentials are redacted from diagnostics and stored run metadata
Explicit alternative configs remain independent and are never merged
Repeated files, directories, stdin, and normalized lexical ordering resolve deterministically
Root and nested manifests preserve declared order
Cycles, duplicates, symlinks, traversal, globs, invalid bytes, and migration overlap are rejected
Exact source hashes and semantic schema hashes remain distinct
Master input rejects DML, transaction control, database operations, client commands, and metadata writes
Create never constructs or opens the configured live target
History and master are independently reconstructed in fresh empty databases
Candidate application converges history to master before atomic save
An unchanged semantic schema creates no migration
Draft migrations retain editable work but cannot apply while marked draft
Operation DAG ordering and cycle diagnostics are deterministic
Rename suggestions do not execute without an exact mapping
Every typed hazard requires an exact SQL-file approval
Unsupported, unobserved, ambiguous, or unverifiable changes fail closed
PostgreSQL strings, identifiers, dollar bodies, nested comments, and savepoints split correctly
SQLite trigger bodies and statements split through SQLite parser APIs
Visible transaction edits are honored and standalone DML is rejected
Metadata, filenames, backend, engine version, ordering, and checksums are validated
Checkpoint state reconciles failure before and after every commit boundary
Completed unit bytes, order, and boundaries are immutable during resume
Exact attempted SQL revisions can be listed and recovered from the database
Generated BEGIN and COMMIT remain visible and no hidden transaction boundary is added
Applied prefix, complete history, and master reconstruction gates run before live writes
Live schema is compared only with its reconstructed applied prefix
Live drift blocks apply and never becomes generated repair SQL
Locks are acquired on pinned ownership and history and drift checks are repeated
Dry-run writes neither target schema nor migration history
Status, create-database, read-only migration directories, and recover behave as documented
Managed table, column, constraint, index, view, and trigger properties round-trip semantically
Native additions and confirmed renames use supported ALTER operations
Transactional rebuilds preserve mapped data, rowids, sequence state, and dependents
Temporary, attached, virtual, shadow, extension-dependent, and unsafe operations are rejected
Writer locking, busy timeout, WAL, rollback journal, and concurrent execution are safe
Online-backup data validation catches row failures without influencing generated SQL
Ordinary rowid, STRICT, and WITHOUT ROWID table properties round-trip
Declared types, defaults, collations, and generated column properties round-trip
Primary, unique, check, and foreign-key constraint properties round-trip
AUTOINCREMENT and accessible rowid state are preserved exactly
Expression and partial index definitions round-trip
View definitions and multi-statement trigger bodies round-trip
All managed PostgreSQL object properties round-trip on every supported major
Create, change, drop, and dependency ordering converge for every managed object
Online phases and transaction-forbidden statements retain visible valid boundaries
External ownership and unsupported or extension-owned effects fail closed
PostgreSQL 15 through 18 and database-creation setting gates are enforced
Managed schemas round-trip with stable logical identities
Enum labels and complete domain definitions round-trip
All sequence properties and ownership relationships round-trip
Ordinary table, column, default, identity, and generated properties round-trip
Primary, unique, check, and foreign-key constraint properties round-trip
Expression, partial, INCLUDE, uniqueness, and method index properties round-trip
View definitions and all managed security options round-trip
Materialized view definitions and population state round-trip
Functions and procedures preserve identity, language, body, and managed attributes
Trigger definitions and managed comments round-trip
Row-level-security flags and policy command, roles, expressions, and permissiveness round-trip
Scratch databases use template0, UUID names, ownership markers, and guarded cleanup
Docker scratch uses labels, random credentials and ports, readiness, and idempotent discovery
Existing-server bootstrap creates only the dedicated role and maintenance database
Expired scratch cleanup removes only entries passing every ownership check
Docker scratch honors a configured custom image without weakening ownership checks
New-major replay independently validates history and master
A no-schema transition gates ordinary create until prepared
Transition apply refuses old targets, version mismatch, and downgrades
Post-upgrade live state must equal reconstruction on the new major
Timeout, cancellation, disconnect, and injected failures clean owned resources
Concurrent executors serialize without stealing ownership
